questions.question: In which of the following dance forms is Mati-Akhora used as the basic exercise pattern that facilitates various dance poses?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mati Akhora **is a set of basic physical exercises used in Sattriya dance, which focuses on building strength, agility, and grace.
 
• These exercises help dancers master complex postures, hand movements, and footwork, laying the groundwork for more advanced dance techniques.
 
• Sattriya is one of the **eight classical dance forms of India**, originating from **Assam.**
 
• It was introduced by the saint-scholar Srimanta Sankardev in the **15th century **as part of the **Vaishnavite **religious practices.
 
• It was traditionally performed by male monks in monasteries (**Sattras**) as a form of devotion, primarily depicting stories from the life of **Lord Krishna.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Eight classical dance forms of India

 Known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork, Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms.

 A dance form characterized by intricate footwork and spins, Kathak focuses on storytelling through expressive movements.
 
 

 **Kuchipudi**

 A combination of dance and drama, Kuchipudi is known for its graceful movements and expressive storytelling.

 Odissi emphasizes fluid torso movements and sculpturesque poses, often depicting stories from Hindu mythology.

 **Sattriya**

 Introduced by Srimanta Sankardev, Sattriya is rooted in Vaishnavism and combines expressive dance, drama, and storytelling.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (2005) provides work for how many days?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• MGNREGA is a landmark social welfare scheme enacted by the Government of India in **2005**.
 
• Its primary objective is to enhance the **livelihood security **of rural households by providing at least **100 days of guaranteed wage employment **each financial year.
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• **Right to Work: **MGNREGA provides rural households the legal right to employment. Any** adult member** of the household willing to do **unskilled **manual labor can apply for work.
 
• **Timely Wages:** Wages are to be paid within **15 days** of the work being completed. The wage rate is determined by the state government in accordance with the Minimum Wage Act.
 
• **Work Availability: **Work must be provided within **15 days** of the demand. If not, the applicant is entitled to an unemployment allowance.
 
• **Decentralized Implementation:** The scheme is implemented through** Gram Panchayats** (local self-government bodies), allowing for local-level decision-making regarding the projects and their implementation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• MGNREGA is a** centrally sponsored scheme**, where the central government provides a significant portion of the funding, especially for wages and material costs, while the state government also contributes.
 
• In some states, the number of guaranteed workdays under MGNREGA has been extended beyond 100 days to counter the impact of economic slowdowns, droughts, or the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• In the **2024 Union Budget**, the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) was allocated** ₹86,000 crore,** the same as the previous year.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Khudai Khidmatgars or the Red Shirts, a powerful non-violent movement?

questions.question: Who elects the Presiding Officer (the speaker) in the State legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Members of Vidhan Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Vidhan Sabha is the** lower house of the State Legislature in India.**
 
• The Speaker is elected from among the **elected members of the Legislative Assembly.**
 
• **Article 168**: It states that there shall be a legislature for each state, which **may consist of a Governor and one or two Houses.**
 
• **Article 173**: It provides the procedure for the **elections of members **of the Legislative Assembly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 163: **It states that the Governor may seek the advice of the Council of Ministers
 
• **Article 164:** It provides for the establishment of a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor in the exercise of his functions. The Chief Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers.
 
• **Article 167:** It outlines the duties of the Chief Minister, including keeping the Governor informed of all decisions of the Council of Ministers
 
• **Article 169:** Abolition or Creation of the Legislative Council.
 
• Article 170: Composition of the Legislative Assemblies.
 
• **Article 171:** Composition of the Legislative Councils.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements best describes Le Chatelier's principle?

A. The law states that the total pressure of a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the individual gases.

<font style="vertical-al
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The principle states that a change in the variables describing a system at equilibrium causes a shift in the equilibrium position to counteract the change.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Le Chatelier's Principle states** that if a system at equilibrium is disturbed by changing the conditions (concentration, temperature, or pressure), the system will adjust itself in a way that counteracts the disturbance and restores a new equilibrium.
 
• The principle is named after** Henri Louis Le Chatelier**, a **French chemist**, who formulated it in the late 19th century.
 
• Le Chatelier's Principle provides** qualitative predictions, not quantitative ones.**
 
• Le Chatelier's Principle guides **how temperature changes affect** equilibrium in exothermic and endothermic reactions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Factors Affecting Equilibrium**

 
• **Concentration**:

 
 
• Increasing the concentration of a reactant shifts the equilibrium towards the products.
 
• Increasing the concentration of a product shifts the equilibrium towards the reactants.
 
 
 
• **Temperature**:
 
 
• For **exothermic reactions**, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium toward the reactants.
 
• For **endothermic reactions**, increasing temperature shifts equilibrium toward the products.
 
 
 
• **Pressure (for gases):**
 
 
• **Increasing pressure** shifts equilibrium towards the side with fewer moles of gas.
 
• **Decreasing pressure** shifts equilibrium toward the side with more moles of gas.
 
 
 
• **Catalysts**:
 
 
• **Catalysts do not affect** the position of equilibrium; they only speed up the rate at which equilibrium is reached.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Kushana dynasty is INCORRECT?

options.text: The Kushanas were a major ruling group in the post-Mauryan period.
Many Kushana rulers also adopted the title ‘devaputra’, or ‘son of god’.
The First Buddhist Council was organised by Kanishka.
Asvaghosha, the author of the Buddhacharita, was the court poet of Kanishka.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__The First Buddhist Council was organised by Kanishka__**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The First Buddhist Council was organized by **Mahakassapa**, with the support of King **Ajatashatru**, the ruler of Magadha.
 
• The First Buddhist Council was held around** 483 BCE**, shortly after the **Parinirvana (death) of Gautama Buddha.**
 
• It took place at **Rajagriha (modern-day Rajgir)** in Bihar, India, at the **Sattapanni Cave** located on the Vebhara Hill.
 
• The main purpose of the council was to** preserve the Buddha’s teachings (Dhamma)** and the **monastic discipline (Vinaya**) after his death.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Kushan Empire was founded by the **Yuezhi**, a nomadic group originally from Central Asia.
 
• They settled in **Bactria** (modern-day Afghanistan) and gradually expanded their power.
 
• **Kanishka I **was the most prominent ruler of the Kushan Empire. His reign is considered the** golden age of the empire**
 
• Under Kanishka, the empire expanded into N**orthern India, including regions like Mathura, Peshawar, and Kashmir.**
 
• The **official language** of the Kushan Empire was **Bactrian**, written in **Greek script**, showing the influence of Hellenistic culture.
 
• The Kushan Empire had diplomatic and trade relations with both the **Roman Empire and the Han Dynasty of China.**
 
• **Roman gold and Chinese silk** were among the goods traded across the empire.

questions.question: The Ryotwari system, devised by Thomas Munro, in which peasant cultivators had to pay annual taxes directly to the government, was prevalent in which of the following present-day states/provinces?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ryotwari system was introduced in Tamil Nadu** during the British colonial period, primarily by the East India Company in the early 19th century.
 
• It was designed by **Sir Thomas Munro**, who was the Governor of Madras (now Chennai).
 
• The Ryotwari system involved **direct revenue collection from the cultivators.**
 
• The** tax rate was usually set at 50%** of the gross produce, but it could vary depending on the crop and local conditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Ryotwari system was introduced in Odisha** during the British rule in the l**ate 19th century, particularly after the Famine of 1866.**
 
• The revenue rates were usually set at around** 25% to 50%** of the estimated yield, depending on the crop type and environmental factors.
 
• The **Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956,** later formalized revenue collection practices and land rights.
 
• **The Ryotwari system was implemented in Punjab** during the British colonial period, particularly **after the First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-1846).**
 
• The **revenue rates **in Punjab were **typically lower **than in some other regions, generally around **30% to 40%** of the produce.
 
• The Ryotwari system in Punjab contributed to agricultural expansion and productivity, particularly in the context of **Green Revolution initiatives in the 1960s and 1970s.**

questions.question: ________is associated with the production and metabolism of fats and steroid hormones.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Smooth endoplasmic reticulum**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER)** is specifically involved in the synthesis of lipids,

 
 
• including fats and steroid hormones, as well as the metabolism of carbohydrates and detoxification of drugs. 
 
 
 
• The SER appears smooth under a microscope because it lacks the ribosomes that give the RER its rough texture.
 
• It is made up of a network of tubules and vesicles, which can vary in shape and size depending on the cell type and its function

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nucleus**:

 
 
• The nucleus is the control center of the cell, containing the cell's genetic material (DNA) and regulating gene expression.
 
• It is responsible for processes such as replication, transcription, and RNA processing.
 
• While the nucleus plays a critical role in regulating metabolic processes through gene expression,
 
 
• it is not directly involved in the production or metabolism of fats and steroid hormones.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Mitochondrion**:
 
 
• Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell, primarily responsible for producing adenosine triphosphate (ATP) through cellular respiration.
 
• They play a significant role in energy metabolism and the oxidative phosphorylation process.
 
• While mitochondria are involved in the metabolism of carbohydrates and proteins,
 
 
• they are not directly responsible for fat production or the synthesis of steroid hormones.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**:
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus is responsible for modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.
 
• It acts as a post-office for the cell, ensuring that proteins and lipids reach their proper destinations.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is involved in the processing of lipids and proteins, but it does not directly produce fats or steroid hormones; instead, it plays a role in their modification and transport after their synthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT come under Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: Promotion of the Welfare of the People

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Promotion of Indian Local Languages**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While the promotion of languages can be seen as a cultural goal, it is not explicitly mentioned as a Directive Principle in the Constitution of India.
 
• Instead, the Constitution recognizes the importance of languages and provides for the protection of the linguistic rights of minorities.
 
• 
 
**Hence **Promotion of Indian Local Languages is ** NOT** come under the Directive Principles of State Policy.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Promotion of the Welfare of the People:
 
 
• This principle emphasizes the government's duty to work towards the overall welfare and well-being of its citizens.
 
• It is a fundamental aspect of the Directive Principles, aiming for social and economic justice.
 
 
 
• **Uniform Civil Code**:
 
 
• The Uniform Civil Code (UCC) is a Directive Principle aimed at ensuring all citizens of India are treated equally under the same set of secular civil laws, regardless of their religion.
 
• It promotes gender equality and social justice.
 
 
 
• **Promotion of Cottage Industries**:
 
 
• This principle encourages the development of small-scale and cottage industries to boost local economies, provide employment, and promote self-reliance
 
• . It is included in the Directive Principles to enhance the livelihood of rural populations.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that the President is eligible for reelection?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 57**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 57
 
 
• **Article 57** of the Indian Constitution deals with the eligibility for re-election to the office of the President of India.
 
• It states that a person who has held, or is currently holding, the office of the **President of India** is **eligible for re-election**.
 
• A President can serve multiple terms if re-elected.
 
• For example, **Dr. Rajendra Prasad**, India's first President, was re-elected and served two consecutive terms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 54:**

 
 
• **​**This article deals with the election of the President.
 
• It establishes the Electoral College, which consists of members of the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and state legislatures.
 
• This article is important because it outlines the process for electing the President.
 
 
 
• **Article 55:**
 
 
• **​** This article outlines the manner of election of the President.
 
• It details the procedure for the Electoral College to cast their votes and the counting of votes.
 
• This article ensures that the President's election is conducted fairly and transparently.
 
 
 
• **Article 56:**
 
 
• This article deals with the term of office of the President and the conditions under which the President can be removed from office.
 
• It does not directly address the President's eligibility for re-election, but it is important for understanding the President's role and tenure.

questions.question: Select the correct statement about climax community

options.text: It is an ecological community in which populations of plants or animals, which are very unstable and exist for very few time.
It is a very first community of ecosystem.
It consist of only plant population that makes a new ecological system.
It is an ecological community in which populations of plants or animals remain stable and exist in balance with each other and their environment.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A climax community is the final stage of ecological succession, where the ecosystem has reached a stable and self-sustaining state.
 
• The species within this community are well-adapted to the local environment and are in balance with each other.
 
• This means that the populations of species in the community are relatively constant over time, and the ecosystem is in balance with its environment.
 
• **Key characteristics of a climax community:**
 
 
• **Stability:** The populations of species remain relatively constant.
 
• **Balance:** The species are well-adapted to the local conditions and interact with each other in a balanced way.
 
• **Self-sufficiency:** The community is able to sustain itself without significant external inputs.
 
• **Resistance:** The community is resistant to change, and it can recover from disturbances.
 
 
 
• A climax community is typically reached through a process called **ecological succession**.
 
• This is a gradual process in which one community of organisms is replaced by another over time.
 
• As the ecosystem develops, the conditions change, and new species become better adapted to the new environment.
 
• Eventually, a stable climax community is reached.

questions.question: Geologically, which of the following physiographic divisions of India is supposed to be one of the most stable land blocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the peninsular plateau**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Peninsular Plateau

 
 
• ​Geologically, the physiographic division of India that is supposed to be one of the most stable land blocks is the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• A tableland made up of ancient crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic rocks are known as the Peninsular plateau.
 
• It belongs to the oldest landmass because it was created by the fracturing and drifting of the Gondwana region.
 
• The vast Deccan Plateau, which can be roughly defined as the peninsular area between these mountain ranges that is south of the Narmada river, is situated between the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats in southern India.
 
• It is a rocky environment highlighted by stones (2,000 ft).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• India's most valuable metal reserves, including those for iron, bauxite, mica, gold, copper, etc., are located in the peninsular plateau.
 
• The peninsular plateau is where renowned mines like Kolar, Bailadila, Singhbum, and Korba are situated.
 
• The peninsular plateau's climate and black soil make it an ideal place for the cultivation of cotton. Since ancient times, cotton has been essential to the trade and economic growth of India.
 
• The peninsular plateau is known for its rough topography and slips.

questions.question: Which ministry started the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Ministry of Labour and Employment**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY)** was launched by the **Ministry of Labour and Employment** in 2016.
 
• The scheme aims to incentivize employers for creating new jobs and expanding the formal employment sector.
 
• Under the scheme:
 
 
• The government pays the **Employer's Pension Scheme (EPS) contribution** (which is 8.33% of the employee's salary) for new employees for a period of three years.
 
• This encourages businesses and employers to hire more workers and increase formal employment, leading to greater job creation in the country.
 
• It is especially focused on benefiting small and medium enterprises by easing the financial burden of employee contributions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ministry of Home Affairs:
 
 
• This ministry is primarily responsible for maintaining internal security and domestic policy, handling issues like law and order, disaster management, and counter-terrorism.
 
• It oversees the management of India's borders, dealing with border security forces, immigration, and border infrastructure.
 
 
 
• Ministry of Corporate Affairs:
 
 
• It regulates the functioning of corporate entities in India, ensuring compliance with the Companies Act and other corporate laws.
 
• The ministry also oversees issues related to corporate governance, transparency, and ethical practices in businesses, along with managing matters related to Insolvency and Bankruptcy.
 
 
 
• Ministry of Rural Development:
 
 
• This ministry focuses on initiatives to improve the living conditions in rural areas, including schemes like Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) for employment and Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana for rural road infrastructure.
 
• It implements various programs aimed at reducing poverty and empowering rural communities through schemes related to housing, water, and sanitation.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from among the following.

options.text: ‘Sanchi Stupa’ is situated in Madhya Pradesh.
‘Bavikonda Stupa’ is situated in Andhra Pradesh.
‘Dhamek Stupa’ is situated in Uttar Pradesh.
Piprahwa Stupa’ is situated in Sikkim.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Piprahwa Stupa is located in **Uttar Pradesh,** near the Nepal border.
 
• This stupa is significant for being one of the sites where **relics of the Buddha** were discovered.
 
• Excavations at Piprahwa revealed **ancient inscriptions and artifacts** that provide insights into early Buddhist culture.
 
• The site is often associated with the historical narrative of the Buddha and the spread of Buddhism in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sanchi Stupa**:

 
 
• Located in** Madhya Pradesh,** it is one of the oldest stone structures in India and a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The stupa is famous for its intricate carvings and is a significant monument of Buddhist architecture.
 
• It was built during the **Mauryan period**, under the reign of Emperor Ashoka.
 
• The site consists of several stupas, temples, and monolithic pillars, showcasing the artistry of ancient Indian craftsmen.
 
 
 
• **Bavikonda Stupa**:
 
 
• Situated in **Andhra Pradesh,** this site is part of the Buddhist heritage in the region.
 
• It is known for its ancient stupas and monastic complex, indicating the spread of Buddhism in South India.
 
• The remains at **Bavikonda include relics, votive stupas**, and other structures dating back to the 3rd century BCE.
 
• The site reflects the influence of trade routes in the propagation of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Dhamek Stupa**:
 
 
• Located in **Uttar Pradesh, near Sarnath**, where Buddha delivered his first sermon after enlightenment.
 
• The stupa is significant for containing relics of the Buddha and is an important pilgrimage site for Buddhists.
 
• It** stands tall with a cylindrical shape**, adorned with intricate carvings that depict various motifs and symbols.
 
• The Dhamek Stupa dates back to the 5th century CE and is an important example of **Gupta architecture.**

questions.question: Who among the following is called 'father of Indian constitution'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhim Rao Ambedkar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bhim Rao Ambedkar is known as the** 'father of the Indian Constitution' **for his pivotal role in drafting the Constitution of India.
 
• He was the **Chairman of the Drafting Committee** and played a crucial role in incorporating fundamental rights and social justice provisions.
 
• Ambedkar** advocated for the rights of marginalized communities** and was a strong proponent of equality and individual rights.
 
• His contributions reflect his deep understanding of social justice, law, and governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **P Subbarayan:**

 
 
• An Indian politician and member of the Indian National Congress who served as a **member of the Constituent Assembly.**
 
• He was instrumental in advocating for the **rights of marginalized communities** but is not primarily associated with the Constitution's drafting.
 
• Subbarayan held various political positions and contributed to the discussions during the framing of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Gopinath Bordoloi:**
 
 
• A prominent Indian politician from Assam who served as the **Chief Minister of Assam.**
 
• He was a member of the Constituent Assembly and played a role in representing the** interests of the northeastern states.**
 
• Bordoloi is known for his **efforts to integrate Assam **into independent India but is not recognized as a key figure in the Constitution's drafting.
 
 
 
• **Rajendra Prasad:**
 
 
• The** first President of India** and a key leader in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He was also a member of the Constituent Assembly and played an important role in the discussions surrounding the Constitution.
 
• Prasad was also the **President of the Constituent Assembly **that drafted the Constitution of India.
 
• He chaired the Constituent Assembly's **committee on food and agriculture.**

questions.question: Atmospheric temperature does NOT depend on _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**salinity of oceans.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Atmospheric temperature **is primarily influenced by air temperature, solar radiation, altitude, latitude, and distance from the sea.
 
• While salinity can affect ocean currents and water temperature, it does not directly impact atmospheric temperature.
 
• Variations in salinity can **influence local weather patterns **but do** not have a direct relationship with atmospheric temperature.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Distance from Sea:**

 
 
• Areas closer to the sea tend to have milder temperatures due to the **moderating effect of water,** which heats up and cools down more slowly than land.
 
• Coastal regions often experience less temperature variation compared to inland areas, which can lead to **higher or lower temperatures** depending on their distance from the ocean.
 
 
 
• **Latitude:**
 
 
• Latitude significantly** affects atmospheric temperature**, with equatorial regions generally experiencing warmer temperatures and polar regions being colder.
 
• The angle of sunlight varies with latitude, **influencing the amount of solar energy** received by different parts of the Earth.
 
 
 
• **Altitude:**
 
 
• As altitude increases,** atmospheric temperature typically decreases due to the thinning of the atmosphere **and reduced air pressure.
 
• Higher elevations tend to have cooler temperatures, regardless of latitude or proximity to the sea.

questions.question: Who among the following was honoured with the title of Khan-i-Khana during the reign of Akbar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bairam Khan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bairam Khan served as a** mentor and guardian **to the young Akbar after the death of his father, Humayun.
 
• He played a crucial role in **consolidating Akbar's power** through military victories.
 
• His contributions were **more military and political **in nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Abul Faz**l

 
 
• Abul Fazl was a prominent historian, best known for writing the **Akbarnama, the official biography of Emperor Akbar.**
 
• He was a close associate of Akbar and served as his chief advisor, significantly influencing policies.
 
• The title Khan-i-Khana means **"Lord of the House,"** reflecting his high status and honor in Akbar's court.
 
• Abul Fazl played a key role in promoting the cultural and intellectual life of the Mughal court, fostering literature and arts.
 
 
 
• **Falcon Brave**:
 
 
• The term "Falcon Brave" does not refer to a historical figure recognized with a specific title during Akbar's reign.
 
• Falcons are often** symbolic of bravery and nobility** in various cultures, but this name is not historically attributed to a person during this period.
 
 
 
• **Todar Mal:**
 
 
• Todar Mal was a notable figure known for his significant contributions to the revenue system under Akbar.
 
• He implemented the **Zabt system**, which was a systematic land revenue assessment, enhancing agricultural productivity.
 
• He did not receive the title of Khan-i-Khana; his contributions were more administrative and fiscal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__ **

 
• Akbar was the **third ruler of the Mughal Empire,** reigning from 1556 to 1605. He is often regarded as one of the greatest Mughal emperors.
 
• Akbar is known for his policy of** Sulh-i-Kul,** which promoted religious tolerance and dialogue among different faiths, including Hinduism, Islam, Jainism, and Christianity.
 
• He **abolished the jizya tax **on non-Muslims and sought to create a syncretic culture.
 
• The construction of iconic structures like** Fatehpur Sikri and the Red Fort** reflects his architectural vision.
 
• Akbar attempted to create a new syncretic religion called** Din-i Ilahi (Religion of God),** aimed at blending the best elements of various religions to promote unity and harmony among his subjects.

questions.question: Identify the Indian musician who is associated with wind instrument (played by blowing).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bismillah Khan.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bismillah Khan was a renowned Indian musician famous for playing the** shehnai,** a traditional wind instrument.
 
• Bismillah Khan played a pivotal role in popularizing the shehnai and is often credited with elevating its status in classical music.
 
• He performed at significant events, including the independence ceremony of India in **1947,** and was **awarded the Bharat Ratna,** India's highest civilian honor.
 
• His contributions to music are celebrated, and he is remembered for his deep emotional expressions through the shehnai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vishwa Mohan Bhat:**

 
 
• A distinguished musician known for playing the **mohan veena, a string instrument.**
 
• He is recognized for his innovative techniques and contributions to Indian classical music, particularly in the slide guitar style.
 
• Vishwa Mohan Bhat has received several awards for his musical prowess but is not associated with wind instruments.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar:**
 
 
• A legendary sitar virtuoso and composer, known for popularizing** Indian classical music globally**.
 
• He collaborated with various international musicians and is renowned for his innovative fusion of Indian and Western music.
 
• Ravi Shankar's instrument is the **sitar, not a wind instrument**.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Deen Dayal:**
 
 
• He was a prominent **Indian politician** and thinker rather than a musician.
 
• Deen Dayal Upadhyaya is known for his contributions to Indian philosophy and politics, particularly in the context of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh.
 
• Deen Dayal Upadhyay's **Integral Humanism **is a philosophy that emphasizes the balance of humans with their surroundings, and the importance of human well-being and social justice.
